summary_of_change:
Operationally, Abercrombie & Fitch is currently delivering solid top-line performance, generating $1,266.7 million in latest quarter revenue (an annualized run-rate of $5,066.8 million) with reported gross margins reaching 71.1%. The Abercrombie adult concept remains the primary growth engine, delivering +8% net sales growth and +4% comparable sales driven by strong demand in tailored workwear, dresses, and denim. Digital omnichannel penetration remains healthy at approximately 45% of net sales, supporting high merchandise margins across its 770 global store footprint.

However, sequential deceleration is emerging beneath the surface. Total company comparable sales flattened to 0.0% in the latest quarter, weighed down by Hollister's slip to -3% comps as teen demand softened against tough prior-year comparisons. Furthermore, the headline operating margin of 19.9% and diluted EPS of $4.17 were heavily flattered by a $100.0 million non-recurring pre-tax IEEPA tariff refund. Excluding this one-time windfall, underlying core operating margin was approximately 12.0%, reflecting genuine operational moderation.

Capital allocation remains heavily focused on returning excess cash to shareholders. ANF generated robust free cash flow and raised full-year share repurchase targets to at least $500 million, having already retired roughly 7% to 9% of outstanding shares year-to-date. With zero debt and $627.7 million in liquid cash, management maintains strong liquidity while continuing to remodel roughly 50 to 60 stores annually into smaller, more productive omnichannel formats.
